Alex P.: Hey team — starting oncall next week, quick Qs: what's the recommended shadow schedule, who do I ping for runbook access, and is there a preferred way to practice handling a P0 without burning real pages? Thanks!

Maya R. (oncall-lead): Welcome! :wave: We'll pair you with a buddy for the first two shifts. Shadow pairing calendar is managed by Oncall Bot (see the auto-post below). DM me if you want an earlier slot or have timezone constraints.

Oncall Bot: Rotation calendar created: https://calendar.company.com/redwood/oncall | Next shadow pair: Alex P. + Samira K. on 2024-11-05 09:00-17:00 (automated notice)

Samira K.: I just granted you read access to /runbooks/oncall and added you to PagerDuty (read-only). You should get an invite email; check spam. Quick tip: from the devbox you can run `rw incident checklist start` to step through the flow interactively.

Ben L.: For low-risk practice, we run tabletop drills in #incidents-sim once a month — will invite you to the next one. Also, short defs: P0 = service down or data loss; P1 = severely degraded. Severity guide: https://redwood.internal/docs/incidents/severity

Alex P.: Awesome — thanks. A couple follow-ups: where exactly are the runbooks (full path), and will VPN be required to view them?

Samira K.: The runbooks live at https://wiki.internal/redwood/runbooks/oncall (VPN or SSO required). If you can't reach it, open a ticket in #help with subject "vpn-access" and include your machine hostname. I also added a short 'first-shift' checklist under your name.

Maya R. (oncall-lead): Short operational checklist when you get a page: 1) Ack in PagerDuty 2) Open incident channel (name prefixed with incident-<id>) 3) Run triage commands 4) Notify stakeholders and set severity. Example quick commands to run right away:
```
kubectl -n inference get pods | grep redwood-runtime
curl -sS http://health.internal/ready
pgrep -a redwood_runtime || echo "no runtime process"
```
If you can't access tools, call me or Ben directly.

Ben L.: Also FYI — alert noise rule: if you see a short <10% CPU blip on a single worker without errors, do not escalate. If CPU spike + errors or increased latency, escalate. When in doubt, ping @Maya R. or @Ben L. in the channel. :thumbsup: 

Alex P.: Good to know. One last thing — post-incident writeups: do we have a template or mandatory fields?

Maya R. (oncall-lead): Yes — use the postmortem template here: https://redwood.internal/postmortems/template.md. Required: timeline, impact, root cause, mitigation, follow-ups owner list, and ETA for fixes. Keep it concise; include links to logs and any alert graphs. I'll review your first write-up.

Alex P.: Perfect. I'll try the `rw incident checklist` tonight and join the tabletop. Thanks everyone, appreciate the quick help! :pray:
